title: Kubernetes Services: Stable Access to Pods

scenes.say: Pods come and go, but your app needs a reliable address. How does Kubernetes solve this?

scenes.label: Service
scenes.sub: A stable IP and DNS name in front of pods.
scenes.say: A Service gives your pods a consistent IP and DNS name, even as pods restart or scale.
ClusterIP is for inside the cluster. NodePort and LoadBalancer let traffic in from outside.

scenes.title: Check Service Endpoints
scenes.say: Check your services with the get service command, and see if any pods are ready with get endpoints.

scenes.question: Does a Service always expose to the internet?
scenes.right: No—ClusterIP is internal only. Use NodePort or LoadBalancer for external access.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Not all services are public. By default, ClusterIP is only reachable inside the cluster.
